PICOSEC Micromegas · 4-pad timing network

Timing resolution with a heteroscedastic neural network

Out-of-fold (10-fold) predictions of the event time from per-pad charge, e-peak amplitude, signal maximum and fitted time. Three scenarios: nominal data, a network trained on nominal data evaluated on data with 10 mV noise, and a network trained and evaluated on the noisy data. All times in picoseconds.

Summary

Double-Gaussian fit of the residual tnetwork − ttrue and of the pull, after the cut |pull| < 5. σtot = √(fcoreσcore² + ftailσtail²), with area fractions.

Method notes

  • Charge. The network inputs are min-max normalised per column. The charge on this page is the real qall_idx value, taken from the ROOT file by the unique event id srs with the same threshold as training (qall < 1 → 0); Q is the sum over the 4 pads. Inverting the normalisation gives the same values (max difference 2·10−5).
  • Predictions. Regenerated from the saved fold models (best_model_fold*.h5) with the training preprocessing. The shuffle and 10-fold split use random_state=1312, so every event is predicted by the model that did not see it. Train-nominal/test-noisy uses the 10-model ensemble with voltage-offset correction; σnetwork combines the mean predicted variance and the spread between models.
  • Fits. Two-pass Gaussian (second pass within ±5σ, binning with best R²). Total resolution and pulls use a double Gaussian with a common mean. Heatmap cells need at least 200 hits.
  • Selection. |pull| < 5 in all scenarios.
